fatal_errors: The proposed tungsten-based HEA coating is unrelated to the target 30% AlFeNiCoCr-bonded ZrB2 cermet consolidated by spark plasma sintering.
Neither cited study tests resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion, so oxidation resistance in air and high-temperature mechanical strength do not establish compatibility with liquid aluminum.
The claim that coherent nanoprecipitates promote a protective oxide scale is not supported by the cited nanoprecipitation paper.
The proposed coating composition, fabrication method, thickness, molten-aluminum temperature, and exposure duration are unspecified, preventing a reproducible material recommendation.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general equipment-corrosion problem and proposes a testable comparison, but it does not reconstruct the target material, processing window, structural mediator, or measured optimum. The target is a bulk ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr cermet whose performance peaks after SPS at 1500 °C because the HEA binder fills pores and bonds ZrB2 grains; excessive heating to 1600 °C causes binder loss and renewed porosity. The generated mechanism instead relies on an unspecified tungsten HEA coating, nanoprecipitation strengthening, and oxide-scale protection. E1 supports mechanical strengthening of a tungsten RHEA, while E2 concerns oxidation of a different RHEA in an oxidizing atmosphere; neither validates corrosion resistance or coating stability in molten aluminum. The proposed exposure experiment could assess the alternative, but its comparator and operating conditions require precise definition.
